strategies.name: User-Initiated Malicious Library Installation via Package Manager (T1204.005)

analytics.name: Analytic 0698
analytics.guidance: User-initiated installation of Python (pip), NodeJS (npm), or other language libraries, followed by unexpected network connections, credential access, or startup file modifications. Defender sees `pip install` or `npm install` commands run by a non-root user, followed shortly by new `.py`, `.sh`, or `.js` files in hidden directories, or interpreter-based execution during boot/login.

tuning.description: Monitored package managers (e.g., pip, npm, gem, poetry, conda)
Directories to watch for post-install execution artifacts (e.g., ~/.local/, /usr/lib/python3.8/site-packages/)
Filter to focus on non-system accounts (e.g., interactive shell users)
Correlate install command to subsequent network/file activity (default: 5 min)

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: execve: Execution of pip, npm, gem, or similar package managers

log_sources.name: auditd:PATH
log_sources.channel: New .py/.js/.sh files written to ~/.local/, ~/.cache/, or /tmp/ within 5 min of package install

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: http::request: Network connection to package registry or C2 from interpreter shortly after install

analytics.name: Analytic 0699
analytics.guidance: Execution of `pip.exe`, `npm.cmd`, or MSI installers within user context, followed by script interpreter startup (e.g., python.exe) or PowerShell with unusual child processes or file writes in `%APPDATA%`, `%TEMP%`, or `%LOCALAPPDATA%`. Defender correlates command-line install tools with Sysmon and Event Logs to trace downstream behavior.

tuning.description: Filter expected automation tools (e.g., enterprise installers, known IDEs)
Used for evaluating if dropped files are packed/obfuscated

analytics.name: Analytic 0700
analytics.guidance: Execution of Homebrew, pip3, npm, or manually downloaded PKGs from Terminal or shell, followed by the creation of startup agents, interpreter spawns, or outbound connections to unfamiliar domains. Defender links Terminal commands to plist creation, unsigned binary launches, and `python3` or `node` processes connecting to remote endpoints.

tuning.description: Filter user persistence plist directories like ~/Library/LaunchAgents
Enable alerting for new binaries lacking Apple or organization signature
Correlate install action to interpreter-based network behavior

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Command line invocation of pip3, brew install, npm install from interactive Terminal

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Creation of new LaunchAgent or LoginItem plist files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents/

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: Outbound HTTP/S initiated by newly installed interpreter process
